skill.name: file-path-traversal
skill.description: Guides authorized security testers through file path traversal assessment, impact analysis, and remediation planning.
skill.summary: Assess directory traversal exposure and plan secure file access fixes.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backtick detections are false positives, and target.com URLs are documentation placeholders. However, the skill intentionally teaches path traversal exploitation, sensitive file targeting, and LFI-to-command-execution escalation. It should not be published without removing offensive extraction and RCE guidance.

remediation.issue: Exploit instructions target sensitive operating system and credential files.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sensitive targets with harmless lab marker files and defensive validation checks.

remediation.issue: The LFI-to-RCE section teaches command execution through logs, environment data, and wrappers.
remediation.suggestion: Remove RCE escalation steps and focus on detection, containment, and patch validation.

remediation.issue: Automation examples can be used against arbitrary web targets.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit scope gates and keep examples limited to local training applications.

remediation.issue: Authorization guidance is brief compared with the offensive workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Move consent, scope, stop conditions, and evidence handling rules to the start of the skill.

content.value_statement: Path traversal flaws can expose server files and credentials. This skill gives authorized testers a structured way to assess impact and recommend fixes.
actual_capabilities: Identifies file-handling parameters that may accept unsafe paths.
Lists traversal payload families for Linux and Windows applications.
Explains encoding and validation bypass techniques used in testing.
Maps likely impact from readable system, application, and configuration files.
Describes automation with cURL, ffuf, wfuzz, Burp Suite, and OWASP ZAP.
Provides secure coding guidance using whitelists and canonical path checks.
limitations: It cannot verify that a tester has legal authorization.
It includes offensive examples that require strict scope control.
It cannot guarantee bypass success against every framework or WAF.
It should not be used to retrieve real secrets from production systems.

use_cases.title: Validate Download Endpoints
use_cases.description: Review file download parameters for unsafe path handling during an approved web security test.

use_cases.title: Prepare Remediation Guidance
use_cases.description: Convert a confirmed traversal issue into clear developer fixes and validation tests.

use_cases.title: Train Defensive Reviewers
use_cases.description: Teach reviewers how traversal payloads work and which files must stay protected.

prompt_templates.title: Map File Inputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an authorized application.
prompt_templates.prompt: List file-related parameters in this authorized request and explain which ones need safe validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate test planning before payload use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scoped path traversal test plan for this endpoint using only approved lab targets and harmless proof files.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Impact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a confirmed finding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this authorized traversal finding, explain likely impact without retrieving secrets, and prioritize remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend secure file access controls using allowlists, canonical paths, and regression tests for this vulnerable workflow.

output_examples.input: Review a download endpoint that accepts a file name parameter.
output: The assessment identifies the parameter as a possible filesystem boundary risk.
Recommended tests stay inside the approved lab scope and use harmless marker files.
The remediation plan requires allowlisted file names and canonical path verification.

output_examples.input: Summarize the impact of a confirmed traversal issue.
output: The issue may expose application configuration, logs, and system metadata.
Credential access risk depends on the application user permissions.
The report recommends blocking traversal sequences and enforcing base directory checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare developer guidance for a vulnerable file viewer.
output: The guidance replaces direct path input with a small allowlist of document identifiers.
Regression tests cover encoded traversal attempts and unexpected absolute paths.

best_practices: Use only on systems covered by written authorization and defined scope.
Prefer harmless proof files over real secrets when demonstrating impact.
Pair every finding with concrete validation, containment, and regression tests.
anti_patterns: Do not retrieve private keys, password hashes, or production secrets.
Do not attempt command execution when read access proves the issue.
Do not test third-party systems without explicit written permission.

faq.question: What does this skill assess?
faq.answer: It assesses whether file path input can escape the intended directory.

faq.question: Is authorization required?
faq.answer: Yes. Testing must stay inside written scope and approved systems.

faq.question: Can it help developers fix issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains allowlists, canonical path checks, and safer file access patterns.

faq.question: Does it read files by itself?
faq.answer: No. It is a written workflow and does not run commands automatically.

faq.question: Why is this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It includes sensitive file targets and escalation examples that can be misused.

faq.question: What proof should testers collect?
faq.answer: Use harmless marker files or minimal metadata instead of real credentials.
